text: To check that labelers were not just accepting invalid critiques, authors of deliberately misleading answers judged the other labelers' critiques. The paper reports assisted labelers found the intended critique 45 ± 5% of the time versus 27 ± 5% without assistance; the fraction of critiques judged valid barely changed (71% vs 73%), while the number of valid critiques rose (0.96 vs 0.62) and valid novel critiques rose (0.24 vs 0.18).
title: Misleading summaries: assisted labelers catch intended flaws 45% vs 27% unassisted
